title: When the Current Wakes
premise: Hazel Sandoval, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Vane brothers—cheerful lenders who collect in blood—takes a salvage contract upriver into monsoon country, where a scientific expedition has gone silent. She finds the expedition's survivors held by a mining syndicate that has bought the local magistrate and claims the river valley as its inheritance, backed by documents stolen from the dead expedition leader. With a leaking boat, a defected syndicate surveyor named Ilya, and the monsoon closing every exit, Hazel must decide whether justice means escaping or burning the syndicate's claim to the waterline. The story ends with Hazel broadcasting the expedition leader's true will over the last working radio, letting the valley's people—not courts, not companies—decide what they inherit, while she rows out ahead of the flood with her debt unpaid and her name finally her own.
about_author: Lena Yarrow is the pen name of a former river guide who spent six seasons on monsoon waterways before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people whose survival depends on reading weather, water, and other people correctly.

chapters.title: Debt Runs Downhill
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In a port town, Hazel repairs her storm-chasing boat under the cheerful eye of Denny Vane, who reminds her of the interest accruing on her father's loan. A salvage broker offers an upriver contract: find the Meridian expedition, silent for eleven days. Emotional beat: cornered pragmatism—she takes the job because stopping costs more.

chapters.title: The Contract and the Current
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She signs papers she barely reads, loads fuel drums, and meets her one crewman, Tuck, who warns that the upper river eats radios first. First monsoon squall hits during departure. Emotional beat: uneasy momentum—the river feels like it already knows something she doesn't.

chapters.title: Static Where Voices Should Be
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Radio contact with the Meridian degrades from clipped coordinates to a single word—'inheritance'—then static. They pass an abandoned checkpoint, magistrate's flag torn down. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into resolve; whatever scared armed men off their own post is upstream.

chapters.title: The Man in the Water
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They pull a half-drowned man from flotsam: Ilya Reyes, a surveyor, who claims he fell from a supply barge. His hands say otherwise—rope burns, a missing boot heel cut deliberately free. Emotional beat: wary suspicion; Hazel doesn't rescue strangers, she acquires liabilities.

chapters.title: What Ilya Knows
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Under pressure, Ilya admits he was the syndicate's land surveyor, hired to redraw the valley's boundaries around a forged inheritance claim signed by the dead expedition leader, Dr. Amara Osei. He ran when he saw what 'relocation' meant. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing; he wants to fix what his maps enabled.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A submerged log opens the hull; they beach at a fishing village where children describe men in company colors taking boats and elders 'for meetings.' Hazel patches the hull with tarpaulin and prayer. Emotional beat: resourcefulness under fear; the villagers' quiet hospitality shames her transactional instincts.

chapters.title: Company Colors
chapters.summary: Tuck's POV. A syndicate patrol skiff boards them; its young officer, Corporal Ennis, is polite and terrified, warning them back downriver 'for insurance reasons.' Tuck notices the patrol boats are running low on fuel too. Emotional beat: the enemy is bigger than guns—it's paperwork and patience.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Ledger
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In a river town, Hazel bribes a clerk and reads the magistrate's ledger: the syndicate, Corvane Extraction, holds a deed dated three days after Dr. Osei's reported death. The dates don't fit the tide tables. Emotional beat: cold clarity—this isn't law, it's forgery wearing law's clothes.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season Is a Character
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. The full monsoon arrives; they shelter in a flooded church where Ilya explains the valley's hydrology—the syndicate's mine tailings dam upstream is failing, and when it goes, everything downstream drowns, including evidence. Emotional beat: ticking clock made physical; nature itself will bury the crime unless someone outruns it.

chapters.title: Meetings with Dangerous Optimists
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Satellite phone call: Denny Vane, delighted, reveals Corvane bought Hazel's debt—he now works for them whether she likes it or not. Bring back Ilya and the original survey plates, and the debt dies. Emotional beat: betrayal by arithmetic; her freedom priced at someone else's erasure.

chapters.title: The Survivor Camp
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Following Osei's last coordinates, they find four Meridian survivors hiding in a karst cave, led by Osei's protégé, Nadia Okonkwo, who carries the doctor's real field journal—and knowledge of where the true will and mineral surveys are hidden. Emotional beat: grief and fury braided together; the expedition wasn't lost, it was hunted.

chapters.title: What the Doctor Left Behind
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Flashback woven through present planning: Osei discovered the valley's rare-earth deposits, refused Corvane's offer, and hid her documentation inside the old mission bell tower—also the village's flood refuge. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined; Osei willed the valley to its people, not to paper.

chapters.title: Ennis Comes Back
chapters.summary: Tuck's POV. Corporal Ennis defects to them, bringing patrol schedules and a confession: he watched Osei's boat get run down and said nothing. Hazel must decide whether a guilty conscience is worth the risk. Emotional beat: moral bookkeeping; Hazel starts believing people can be more than their worst entry.

chapters.title: The Bell Tower Run
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Racing a rising river, they reach the mission and retrieve Osei's sealed case—true will, unaltered surveys, correspondence proving the forgery—as Corvane gunboats enter the bend behind them. Emotional beat: triumph curdling instantly into pursuit; the prize makes them targets.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Confluence
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. Corvane traps them at the river confluence; Tuck is shot covering the escape, and Ilya surrenders himself as bait so the others can slip into flooded backchannels. Emotional beat: sacrifice without heroics—Ilya pays against his own ledger.

chapters.title: Interrogation on the Barge
chapters.summary: Ilya's POV. On Corvane's command barge, Ilya faces the regional director, Ms. Ashgrave, who offers him his old life back and explains, reasonably, why the valley's people are a rounding error. Emotional beat: seduction of power; Ilya understands exactly how he was first recruited.

chapters.title: The Dam Groans
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hiding in the mangroves, Hazel hears the tailings dam begin to fail—a deep structural groan rolling across the water. Evacuating downstream villages becomes impossible if they spend time on revenge. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—justice that costs the innocent isn't justice.

chapters.title: Broadcasting the Dead Woman's Will
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. From the mission tower's radio, Hazel reads Osei's will and the forgery evidence on every frequency, then hands copies to village elders and Ennis's sympathetic officers. Ashgrave's authority dissolves as her own patrols start listening. Emotional beat: power shifting from paper to people; the law arrives late but arrives.

chapters.title: When the Current Wakes
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The dam fails. Hazel pilots the overloaded boat through the surge, saving whom she can, losing the salvage cargo and with it any payment. Ashgrave's barge, heavy with seized ore, founders; Ennis pulls survivors from the water regardless of allegiance. Emotional beat: cathartic chaos—the river settles every account its own way.

chapters.title: Afterwater
chapters.summary: Nadia's POV. Days later: relief boats, a magistrate arrested with his ledger, Corvane's claim voided pending investigation. Nadia begins cataloguing Osei's legacy with the elders. Emotional beat: mourning with purpose; inheritance means stewardship, not possession.

chapters.title: The Vane Brothers' Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Denny Vane arrives to collect, finds no salvage, no Ilya in custody, and a valley full of witnesses who know his new employers' name. Hazel offers him the only asset left: her testimony, kept quiet as long as the debt stays quiet. Emotional beat: quiet victory; she beats dangerous optimists with their own currency—leverage.

chapters.title: Moving Water
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Repaired, repainted, renamed after Dr. Osei, the boat heads downriver. Hazel could stop now—debt frozen, name cleared—but the horizon shows storm cells stacking, and somewhere needs a chaser who reads water. Emotional beat: earned restlessness; she keeps moving not because stopping costs more, but because moving finally costs nothing.
